presets.label: Visual moodboard
presets.intent: Translate the natural-fabric and simple-uniform philosophy into an art-directed visual system.
presets.prompt: Create an editorial visual moodboard titled THE NATURAL UNIFORM. Art direction: tactile, masculine, understated, analog, slightly cinematic. Use a warm cream, washed-denim blue, tobacco brown, charcoal, olive, and black-leather palette. Build an asymmetric magazine collage with large typographic statements, color swatches, CSS-made fabric textures for linen, denim, wool, leather, and suede, outfit silhouette panels, material labels, and seasonal notes. Core ideas: denim plus a good tee; natural fibers over synthetics; clean trousers; loafers year-round; leather and linen as contrast; buy quality basics and ignore trend churn. No ecommerce chrome. Make the page feel like a creative director's working board, not a generic dashboard.
acceptance: Includes palette, material textures, silhouettes, and editorial principles
Asymmetric collage remains readable on mobile
Visual hierarchy feels like a fashion magazine
Uses no external image or font URLs

presets.label: Product detail page
presets.intent: Turn the material-first philosophy into a credible premium product experience.
presets.prompt: Create a premium product detail page for THE FIELD OVERSHIRT, a tobacco-brown linen and cotton layer priced at $168. Use editorial menswear art direction: warm cream canvas, deep charcoal type, washed denim accents, restrained rules, tactile CSS texture panels, and generous whitespace. Include a CSS-art product gallery with thumbnails, product title and price, color swatches, size selection, add-to-wardrobe button, natural-fiber composition, fit notes, care, shipping, and a styling formula pairing it with a white tee, medium-wash denim, brown belt, and suede loafers. Include a compact mobile purchase bar. Avoid generic SaaS styling.
acceptance: Product gallery, variants, sizing, price, and purchase action are present
Material and fit information are prominent
Mobile purchase action remains reachable
Buttons and selectors have visible interaction states

presets.label: Seasonal lookbook
presets.intent: Express the same wardrobe fundamentals through seasonal progression.
presets.prompt: Create an editorial lookbook called SUMMER INTO FALL. Show four full-width CSS-art looks that progress from hot-weather linen to darker denim, suede, leather, and chunky knit layers. Use oversized look numbers, concise outfit formulas, material callouts, a cream-to-charcoal color progression, and horizontal editorial rules. Include: jeans and tee summer; Johnny-collar polo with linen shorts; overshirt with medium denim and suede loafers; fall Henley with leather jacket and boots. Make scrolling feel cinematic and keep mobile compositions intentional.
acceptance: Contains four distinct seasonal looks
Every look has an outfit formula and material callouts
Color progression communicates the seasonal transition
Mobile layout preserves editorial sequencing

presets.label: Capsule wardrobe
presets.intent: Make the quality-basics philosophy useful as a bounded wardrobe system.
presets.prompt: Create a shoppable editorial guide titled THE 12-PIECE NATURAL WARDROBE. Present a disciplined capsule: white tee, black tee, Henley, knit polo, linen shirt, overshirt, light denim, dark denim, linen trouser, loafers, white sneaker, and leather jacket. Use a numbered modular grid, material badges, palette chips, outfit-combination counter, and three occasion formulas for coffee, hot-weather gathering, and drinks. Art direction is quiet luxury without luxury clichés: cream paper, serif headlines, olive and tobacco accents, crisp black rules.
acceptance: Exactly twelve wardrobe building blocks are shown
Natural material information is visible
Includes at least three occasion formulas
Grid collapses cleanly without losing numbering

presets.label: Editorial style guide
presets.intent: Convert the source advice into a readable long-form visual essay.
presets.prompt: Create a long-form editorial feature titled FIT, FABRIC, FORMULA. Open with a bold thesis about simple clothes worn well. Build chapters for natural fibers, the denim-and-tee uniform, trousers that fall cleanly, seasonal layering, footwear, and situational dressing. Use pull quotes, diagrams made with CSS, fabric comparison cards, marginal notes, and a sticky chapter index. Palette: newsprint cream, ink black, denim blue, tobacco, and muted olive. Typography should feel like an independent fashion journal.
acceptance: Includes all six editorial chapters
Sticky index provides useful navigation
Pull quotes and diagrams break up long text
Reading width and contrast remain accessible

presets.label: Collection grid
presets.intent: Apply the same material hierarchy to a browseable commerce collection.
presets.prompt: Create a collection page titled SHOP BY MATERIAL for a menswear store. Organize products under Linen, Cotton, Wool, Denim, Leather, and Suede using tactile CSS-art thumbnails, product names, prices, material percentages, and quick-add controls. Add filters for season, occasion, color, and fit plus a short manifesto explaining why natural fibers age well. Use cream, charcoal, washed blue, olive, and brown; keep controls elegant and editorial rather than dashboard-like.
acceptance: Six material groups are represented
Product cards include price and composition
Filter controls are keyboard accessible
Collection grid adapts from desktop to mobile
